raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Overview

Fixes #60340. In streaming mode `Olmo3ReasoningBuffer.add_text` decides whether to hold a delta back using `string_overlap(delta_text, marker)`, and that helper reports *containment* as an overlap: any delta that merely occurs inside `<think>` / `</think>` (`think`, `in`, `k`, `>`, `/`, ...) is buffered as if it could start a marker. Two consequences:

- Mid stream the delta is needlessly delayed by one step.
- If generation ends on such a delta the buffered text is never emitted, because nothing flushes the buffer at end of stream, so streaming loses trailing content that the non-streaming path returns (repro in the issue, verified locally against current main).

`abstract_parser.py` is touched on purpose, and the repo guidance says to call that out: the missing end-of-stream flush is wrong for every legacy `ReasoningParser` with a string hold-back buffer, not just olmo3, so `finalize_generation` now gives any legacy parser that defines `finish_streaming` one chance to flush at `finished=True`. The hook is opt-in via `getattr`, engine-based parsers still flush through `_flush_engine_parsers`, and no existing parser's behavior changes except olmo3 opting in.

## Claims

- The buffer holds a delta only while its tail can still grow into a marker (a suffix of the buffer that is a proper prefix of `<think>` / `</think>`); a delta that merely occurs inside a marker streams through immediately. `string_overlap`, now unused, is removed.
- New `Olmo3ReasoningParser.finish_streaming()` drains the buffer at end of stream: held text goes out as content once the reasoning block closed, and as reasoning while it is still open, matching what earlier deltas already streamed.
- `finalize_generation` calls a legacy reasoning parser's `finish_streaming` when defined; engine-based parsers (`engine_based_streaming=True`) are untouched and flush via the existing path.

Non-streaming extraction, `is_reasoning_end`, and the token-id logic are unchanged, so model outputs/accuracy are not affected; no model eval was run for that reason.

## Validation

```bash
python -m pytest tests/reasoning/test_olmo3_reasoning_parser.py -q
python -m pytest tests/parser/ -q --ignore=tests/parser/cohere
python -m pytest tests/reasoning/ -q
```

- 19 passed in the olmo3 file (15 existing pins plus 4 new: the issue repro with the exact chunk sequence, a genuine marker-prefix tail flushed as content, unterminated reasoning flushed as reasoning, and a buffer unit test for the tightened hold).
- 6307 passed + 384 subtests in tests/parser (cohere collection skipped locally: `cohere_melody` is not installed in this environment), including the new `test_parse_delta_finished_flushes_legacy_reasoning_holdback` which wires a hold-back legacy parser through `parse_delta(finished=True)` and pins the flush plus no-double-flush.
- 486 passed in tests/reasoning.
- The issue's repro script prints `'That is what I '` (loss) before and `'That is what I think'` (parity) after.
- `ruff check` and `ruff format --check` clean on the four touched files.

## Follow-up tests in `c24c5e1033`

The review that verified this change named two gaps, and both are now covered on top of the head above. The numbers in the list above belong to `920b0c4778`; only the two test files were rerun for this follow-up.

- `test_char_level_streaming_holds_only_marker_characters` feeds the issue sequence one character at a time and asserts that no character of the reasoning or the content is ever held back, with a running check that what has streamed is always a prefix of the final output.
- `test_contained_delta_streams_in_the_call_that_fed_it` pins that a delta which occurs inside a marker but cannot grow into one comes back from the call that fed it rather than the next chunk.
- `test_parse_delta_contained_marker_substring_streams_mid_stream` pins the same property through `DelegatingParser.parse_delta`, so the coverage is not only against the reasoning parser directly.

All three fail on the parent. The char-level run stops at `('R', 'That is what I ')` against `('R', 'That is what I think')`, so the trailing `think` is dropped outright, and the contained delta returns `None` at both the parser and the facade level.

`tests/reasoning/test_olmo3_reasoning_parser.py` together with `tests/parser/test_streaming.py` is 43 passed on this head, and `pre-commit run --files` on the two changed test files is clean across ruff, typos, check-test-tethering and mypy 3.10. The other mypy version hooks did not run in this environment.

Duplicate check: no comments on #60340, no open PR references it, and the adjacent olmo3 PRs (#56262, #55210) predate the buffer and cover different boundaries.

AI assistance: this change was prepared with AI assistance (Kimi Code); I reviewed every changed line and ran the test commands above.

nodes.body:
@xiaohaifeng1999 thank you for the independent run, and for naming the two gaps instead of only reporting the numbers. Both are covered in `c24c5e1033`, which is test-only on top of the head you reviewed.

The char-level probe feeds the issue sequence one character at a time and asserts that no character of the reasoning or the content is ever held back. What it pins down is the latency, not just the final text: after every character, what has streamed so far has to be a prefix of the final output, so nothing is carried into a later chunk. The only characters allowed to produce no delta are the markers' own.

The message-level check is the contained-delta case you called out. `think` fed after `</think` has closed cannot grow into a marker, so it has to come back from the call that fed it. That one is pinned twice: once against `Olmo3ReasoningParser` directly, and once through `DelegatingParser.parse_delta`, which closes your caveat about the harness going around the facade. The facade version feeds explicit chunks rather than tokenizing, so it controls the chunk boundaries the way your probes do.

Both fail on the parent, and they fail the way you would expect. The char-level run stops at `('R', 'That is what I ')` against `('R', 'That is what I think')`, so the trailing `think` is dropped outright rather than merely delayed. The contained delta returns `None` at both levels.

On your two caveats. Non-streaming behavior for unterminated reasoning is unchanged and I have left it alone, since the PR is about what reaches the client while the stream is open. The facade gap is now covered. I will take you up on the script if you still want to share it; a char-level probe through the real tokenizer, as opposed to my stub vocab, is the one thing my tests do not give you.

Local CPU, macOS. `tests/reasoning/test_olmo3_reasoning_parser.py` and `tests/parser/test_streaming.py` are 43 passed on this head, and `pre-commit run --files` on the two changed test files is clean across ruff, typos, check-test-tethering and mypy 3.10. The three added tests are red on the parent and green here.

## Claude Code Review

This pull request is from a fork — automated review is disabled. A repository maintainer can comment `@claude review` to run a one-time review.

Verified offline at the parser level: explicit chunk sequences fed to `extract_reasoning_streaming` with a dummy tokenizer, no model or server. Same probes on `main` (262eefc9f2) and this head (920b0c4778):

| case | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| issue #60340 sequence | final `think` delta held, never emitted (`That is what I `) | complete; `think` arrives in its own delta |
| same text, one char per delta | chars inside a marker are held; trailing `think` lost | only the two markers' own characters are consumed; every character of the text streams |
| contained delta + follow-up chunk | held, then merged into the next delta (one-chunk latency) | emitted immediately |
| trailing true prefix of `</think>` | lost | drained by `finish_streaming()` as content |
| unterminated reasoning ending on a contained delta | lost entirely | emitted immediately as reasoning |

The buffer now holds a delta only while its tail can still grow into a marker (`_tail_awaiting_marker`); a delta that merely occurs inside a marker streams through. In the char-level run, deltas with no visible output drop from 25 to 15: the 15 are the two markers' own characters, and the 10 content deltas `main` held back now ship with their own delta. A second `finish_streaming()` emits nothing. The PR's tests already pin the parser-level double drain, and my run reproduces that; the `parse_delta(finished=True)` path, which my harness does not exercise, is covered by the new `test_parse_delta_finished_flushes_legacy_reasoning_holdback` (including its no-repeated-reasoning-flush assertion).

`olmo3_tool_parser.py` is unchanged (same hash), and the tool-side probes are byte-identical on this head vs `main`. The only implementation change outside the Olmo3 parser is the opt-in hook in `vllm/parser/abstract_parser.py`: it calls `finish_streaming` only on a legacy reasoning parser that defines it, skips `engine_based_streaming=True`, and Olmo3 is the only shipped legacy reasoning parser that defines it. The engine-side adapters/engine and `k2_horizon_tool_parser` are either skipped by that guard or never consulted, so no other parser's behavior changes today.

Two caveats: non-streaming behavior for unterminated reasoning is unchanged (everything comes back as content, as before), and my harness calls the parser directly rather than through the facade. The new tests cover the issue sequence, the prefix-tail flush, and an unterminated flush; the fifth case is related but not identical — that test flushes a prefix tail, while mine is a contained delta that streams through. The char-level probe and the message-level mid-stream check are what I'd add; happy to share the script.

(These runs were AI-assisted; raw logs are available for both SHAs.)

 from vllm.parser.abstract_parser import DelegatingParser
 from vllm.parser.engine.registered_adapters import Qwen3ParserReasoningAdapter

     )
     assert json.loads(tool_args) == {"city": city}
     assert content == ""
+
+
+class HoldbackThinkReasoningParser(ThinkReasoningParser):
+    """Legacy parser that holds every reasoning delta back, flushable at end.
+
+    Stands in for legacy parsers with a string buffer (e.g. olmo3) whose
+    held-back tail only surfaces when the serving layer asks for it.
+    """
+
+    def __init__(self, *args, **kwargs):
+        super().__init__(*args, **kwargs)
+        self._held: list[str] = []
+
+    def extract_reasoning_streaming(self, *args, **kwargs):
+        delta = super().extract_reasoning_streaming(*args, **kwargs)
+        if delta is not None and delta.reasoning:
+            self._held.append(delta.reasoning)
+            delta.reasoning = None
+            if delta.content is None and not delta.tool_calls:
+                delta = None
+        return delta
+
+    def finish_streaming(self):
+        if not self._held:
+            return None
+        text = "".join(self._held)
+        self._held.clear()
+        return DeltaMessage(reasoning=text)
+
+
+def test_parse_delta_finished_flushes_legacy_reasoning_holdback(tokenizer, request_obj):
+    # finalize_generation must give a legacy reasoning parser that defines
+    # finish_streaming one chance to flush its held-back tail at stream end.
+    class TestParser(DelegatingParser):
+        reasoning_parser_cls = HoldbackThinkReasoningParser
+        tool_parser_cls = None
+
+    parser = TestParser(tokenizer)
+    text = "<think>let me think</think>the answer"
+    results = stream_text(parser, tokenizer, text, request_obj)
+    reasoning, content, _ = collect_fields(results)
+    assert reasoning == ""
+    assert content == "the answer"
+
+    final = parser.parse_delta("", [], request_obj, finished=True)
+    assert final is not None
+    assert final.reasoning == "let me think"
+
+    # no double flush on a repeated finished call
+    again = parser.parse_delta("", [], request_obj, finished=True)
+    assert again is None or not again.reasoning
+
+
+class _Olmo3VocabTokenizer:
+    """Just enough vocab for Olmo3ReasoningParser's think_end splits."""
+
+    def get_vocab(self):
+        return {"Ġ</": 1, "</": 2, "think": 3, ">": 4}
+
+
+def test_parse_delta_contained_marker_substring_streams_mid_stream(request_obj):
+    # The same no-latency property one layer up, through the facade rather
+    # than against the reasoning parser directly: a delta that occurs inside
+    # a marker but cannot grow into one must come back from the parse_delta
+    # call that fed it, not ride along with the next chunk.
+    class TestParser(DelegatingParser):
+        reasoning_parser_cls = Olmo3ReasoningParser
+        tool_parser_cls = None
+
+    parser = TestParser(_Olmo3VocabTokenizer())
+    prev = ""
+
+    def step(chunk):
+        nonlocal prev
+        message = parser.parse_delta(chunk, [], request_obj, finished=False)
+        prev += chunk
+        return message
+
+    step("<think>")
+    assert step("R").reasoning == "R"
+    step("</")
+    step("think")
+    step(">")
+    assert step("plain ").content == "plain "
+
+    contained = step("think")
+    assert contained is not None, "contained delta was held back at the facade"
+    assert contained.content == "think"
+
+    assert step("ing done").content == "ing done"
+
+    final = parser.parse_delta("", [], request_obj, finished=True)
+    assert final is None or not final.content

+class _TinyTokenizer:
+    """Just enough vocab for Olmo3ReasoningParser's think_end splits."""
+
+    def get_vocab(self):
+        return {"Ġ</": 1, "</": 2, "think": 3, ">": 4}
+
+
+def _stream(parser, chunks):
+    reasoning, content, prev = "", "", ""
+    for chunk in chunks:
+        message = parser.extract_reasoning_streaming(
+            prev, prev + chunk, chunk, [], [], []
+        )
+        prev += chunk
+        if message is not None:
+            reasoning += message.reasoning or ""
+            content += message.content or ""
+    return reasoning, content
+
+
+def test_streaming_does_not_hold_a_delta_that_merely_occurs_in_a_marker():
+    # #60340: "think" is a substring of "<think>"/"</think>" but cannot grow
+    # into one here, so it must stream like any other text.
+    parser = Olmo3ReasoningParser(_TinyTokenizer())
+    chunks = ["<think>", "R", "</", "think", ">", "That is what I ", "think"]
+    reasoning, content = _stream(parser, chunks)
+    assert reasoning == "R"
+    assert content == "That is what I think"
+    assert parser.finish_streaming() is None
+
+
+def test_finish_streaming_flushes_a_tail_still_awaiting_a_marker():
+    # The stream can genuinely end on a marker prefix ("</"); at that point
+    # the held tail is emitted as content, like the non-streaming path.
+    parser = Olmo3ReasoningParser(_TinyTokenizer())
+    chunks = ["<think>", "R", "</", "think", ">", "That is what I ", "</"]
+    reasoning, content = _stream(parser, chunks)
+    assert (reasoning, content) == ("R", "That is what I ")
+    flushed = parser.finish_streaming()
+    assert flushed is not None
+    assert flushed.content == "</"
+    assert flushed.reasoning is None
+    # draining is idempotent: a second finish has nothing left to say
+    assert parser.finish_streaming() is None
+
+
+def test_finish_streaming_flushes_unterminated_reasoning_as_reasoning():
+    # If the stream ends mid-reasoning, earlier deltas already went out as
+    # reasoning, so the held tail stays reasoning for stream consistency.
+    parser = Olmo3ReasoningParser(_TinyTokenizer())
+    reasoning, content = _stream(parser, ["<think>", "R", "</"])
+    assert (reasoning, content) == ("R", "")
+    flushed = parser.finish_streaming()
+    assert flushed is not None
+    assert flushed.reasoning == "</"
+    assert flushed.content is None
+
+
+def test_buffer_holds_only_a_genuine_marker_prefix():
+    buffer = Olmo3ReasoningBuffer()
+    # "think" occurs inside "<think>" but is not its start: no hold
+    assert buffer.add_text("think") is not None
+    assert len(buffer) == 0
+    # "</" can still complete into "</think>": held
+    assert buffer.add_text("</") is None
+    assert len(buffer) == 2
+    # completing the marker flushes the buffer
+    buffer.add_text("think>")
+    assert len(buffer) == 0
+
+
+def test_char_level_streaming_holds_only_marker_characters():
+    # One character per delta. A character of the reasoning or the content
+    # must surface in the call that fed it; only the markers' own characters
+    # are allowed to produce no delta while they are still ambiguous.
+    text = "<think>R</think>That is what I think"
+    # "<think>" is text[0:6], "R" is text[6:7], "</think>" is text[7:15]
+    marker_spans = set(range(0, 6)) | set(range(7, 15))
+
+    parser = Olmo3ReasoningParser(_TinyTokenizer())
+    reasoning, content, prev = "", "", ""
+    silent: list[int] = []
+    for i, ch in enumerate(text):
+        message = parser.extract_reasoning_streaming(prev, prev + ch, ch, [], [], [])
+        prev += ch
+        if message is None:

+            continue
+        reasoning += message.reasoning or ""
+        content += message.content or ""
+        # never behind: what has streamed is a prefix of the final text, so
+        # no character is carried over into a later chunk
+        assert "R".startswith(reasoning)
+        assert "That is what I think".startswith(content)
+
+    assert (reasoning, content) == ("R", "That is what I think")
+    assert set(silent) <= marker_spans
+    assert not set(silent) & set(range(15, len(text)))
+    assert parser.finish_streaming() is None
+
+
+def test_contained_delta_streams_in_the_call_that_fed_it():
+    # A delta that occurs inside a marker but cannot grow into one ("think"
+    # after "</think" already closed, or in plain content) must come back in
+    # its own call, not be merged into whatever chunk follows it.
+    parser = Olmo3ReasoningParser(_TinyTokenizer())

+    step("</")
+    step("think")
+    step(">")

+    contained = step("think")
+    assert contained is not None, "contained delta was held back"
+    assert contained.content == "think"

+    follow_up = step("ing done")
+    assert follow_up is not None
+    assert follow_up.content == "ing done"

issue_comments.body:
@xiaohaifeng1999 thank you for the independent run, and for naming the two gaps instead of only reporting the numbers. Both are covered in `c24c5e1033`, which is test-only on top of the head you reviewed.

The char-level probe feeds the issue sequence one character at a time and asserts that no character of the reasoning or the content is ever held back. What it pins down is the latency, not just the final text: after every character, what has streamed so far has to be a prefix of the final output, so nothing is carried into a later chunk. The only characters allowed to produce no delta are the markers' own.

The message-level check is the contained-delta case you called out. `think` fed after `</think` has closed cannot grow into a marker, so it has to come back from the call that fed it. That one is pinned twice: once against `Olmo3ReasoningParser` directly, and once through `DelegatingParser.parse_delta`, which closes your caveat about the harness going around the facade. The facade version feeds explicit chunks rather than tokenizing, so it controls the chunk boundaries the way your probes do.

Both fail on the parent, and they fail the way you would expect. The char-level run stops at `('R', 'That is what I ')` against `('R', 'That is what I think')`, so the trailing `think` is dropped outright rather than merely delayed. The contained delta returns `None` at both levels.

On your two caveats. Non-streaming behavior for unterminated reasoning is unchanged and I have left it alone, since the PR is about what reaches the client while the stream is open. The facade gap is now covered. I will take you up on the script if you still want to share it; a char-level probe through the real tokenizer, as opposed to my stub vocab, is the one thing my tests do not give you.

Local CPU, macOS. `tests/reasoning/test_olmo3_reasoning_parser.py` and `tests/parser/test_streaming.py` are 43 passed on this head, and `pre-commit run --files` on the two changed test files is clean across ruff, typos, check-test-tethering and mypy 3.10. The three added tests are red on the parent and green here.

## Claude Code Review

This pull request is from a fork — automated review is disabled. A repository maintainer can comment `@claude review` to run a one-time review.

Verified offline at the parser level: explicit chunk sequences fed to `extract_reasoning_streaming` with a dummy tokenizer, no model or server. Same probes on `main` (262eefc9f2) and this head (920b0c4778):

| case | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| issue #60340 sequence | final `think` delta held, never emitted (`That is what I `) | complete; `think` arrives in its own delta |
| same text, one char per delta | chars inside a marker are held; trailing `think` lost | only the two markers' own characters are consumed; every character of the text streams |
| contained delta + follow-up chunk | held, then merged into the next delta (one-chunk latency) | emitted immediately |
| trailing true prefix of `</think>` | lost | drained by `finish_streaming()` as content |
| unterminated reasoning ending on a contained delta | lost entirely | emitted immediately as reasoning |

The buffer now holds a delta only while its tail can still grow into a marker (`_tail_awaiting_marker`); a delta that merely occurs inside a marker streams through. In the char-level run, deltas with no visible output drop from 25 to 15: the 15 are the two markers' own characters, and the 10 content deltas `main` held back now ship with their own delta. A second `finish_streaming()` emits nothing. The PR's tests already pin the parser-level double drain, and my run reproduces that; the `parse_delta(finished=True)` path, which my harness does not exercise, is covered by the new `test_parse_delta_finished_flushes_legacy_reasoning_holdback` (including its no-repeated-reasoning-flush assertion).

`olmo3_tool_parser.py` is unchanged (same hash), and the tool-side probes are byte-identical on this head vs `main`. The only implementation change outside the Olmo3 parser is the opt-in hook in `vllm/parser/abstract_parser.py`: it calls `finish_streaming` only on a legacy reasoning parser that defines it, skips `engine_based_streaming=True`, and Olmo3 is the only shipped legacy reasoning parser that defines it. The engine-side adapters/engine and `k2_horizon_tool_parser` are either skipped by that guard or never consulted, so no other parser's behavior changes today.

Two caveats: non-streaming behavior for unterminated reasoning is unchanged (everything comes back as content, as before), and my harness calls the parser directly rather than through the facade. The new tests cover the issue sequence, the prefix-tail flush, and an unterminated flush; the fifth case is related but not identical — that test flushes a prefix tail, while mine is a contained delta that streams through. The char-level probe and the message-level mid-stream check are what I'd add; happy to share the script.

(These runs were AI-assisted; raw logs are available for both SHAs.)
